title: Choose the visual world for the Universal Relocations home page
question: The roll assigned The Bill of Lading. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every option stays light, navy #00056E and orange #FEA70E.

options.label: The Bill of Lading
options.lineage: Ocean bills of lading and customs forms: the paper Universal issues as an FMC-licensed NVOCC
options.thesis: The home page is the document that moves your life: you request a quote by filling in a bill of lading.
materials: numbered field boxes on hairline rules
options.viewport: A full-width form with numbered boxes for From, To, move date and home size. Filling it in is the quote request, and an orange RECEIVED stamp lands when you submit.
options.risk: It can feel bureaucratic if the form is set timidly or the boxes get cramped.

raised.raise: Printed in exactly two spot inks, navy and orange, that overprint where they cross, like a real two-colour form.
Orange is reserved for the stamp and the primary action. Every structural line is a 1px navy hairline.
Every region locks to one field-box module, so the whole page aligns like a single printed form.
Quote and shipment states share one vocabulary: Received, Surveyed, Packed, Cleared, Afloat, Delivered.

options.label: The Bag Tag
options.lineage: Airline baggage tags and IATA three-letter airport codes
options.thesis: Your move as one tag that follows everything from EWR to MAA: one partner, door to door.
options.viewport: A giant tag spans the hero. Origin and destination codes are the headline, and the quote fields are printed on the tag.
options.risk: It's familiar travel imagery that airlines use a lot, and it hints at flying luggage more than ocean freight.

options.label: The Carton Wall
options.lineage: Sneaker archive box stacks, fused with labelled moving cartons
options.thesis: Services and hubs as a wall of labelled cartons. Pull one out to open it.
options.viewport: A stacked wall of cartons, each end label naming a service. The quote carton sits pulled half out at eye level.
options.case: Fuses well because everyone who moves knows the labelled carton. It loses narrowly on clarity for the international, one-partner story.
options.risk: It reads like a local moving company rather than an international one.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: The move as numbered, exploded assembly steps.
options.viewport: Numbered steps with a parts inventory.
options.risk: Too playful for a high-stakes move.
options.case: Fuses poorly: families and diplomats don't see their move as a toy kit.
options.kept: One strict alignment module for every region.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Moves presented as printed plates with registration marks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it reads as a portfolio, not a mover.
options.kept: One accent used only as the seal; hairline-built grid.

options.label: Treasure Map
options.thesis: Navigation as inference on weathered vellum.
options.viewport: A weathered map with a hidden route.
options.risk: False trails contradict a promise of certainty.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a mover must remove guesswork, not stage it.
options.kept: A named state vocabulary for every stage.

options.label: Risograph Print
options.thesis: Spot inks misregistering over toothy paper.
options.risk: Zine energy undercuts trust for big-ticket moves.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it lacks the authority a customs-and-freight partner needs.
options.kept: Two spot inks that overprint where they cross.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Six luminous gauges you trust in the dark.
options.viewport: Six gauges as the move's status.
options.risk: A dark theme breaks the light-theme brief.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark cockpit conflicts with the pinned light theme.
options.kept: Every reading shows trend as well as value.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What international movers ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A full-width photo hero with a quote form beside the headline, then services, stats, reviews and hubs.
canonCard.risk: It's indistinguishable from competing movers by design.
